## Summary

2-Butoxynaphthalene. This is sample data; the quantities are not experimentally verified.

## Reagents

| Reagent | CAS | MW (g/mol) | Amount | mmol | Equiv |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2-Naphthol | 135-19-3 | 144.17 | 1.442 g | 10.0 | 1.0 |
| 1-Bromobutane | 109-65-9 | 137.02 | 1.644 g | 12.0 | 1.2 |
| Sodium hydroxide | 1310-73-2 | 40.00 | 0.480 g | 12.0 | 1.2 |
| Ethanol | 64-17-5 | 46.07 | 25 mL; plus some for recrystallisation | – | – |
| Ethyl acetate | 141-78-6 | 88.11 | 30 mL | – | – |
| Sodium sulfate | 7757-82-6 | 142.04 | 2 g | – | – |

## Procedure

1. Charge 2-naphthol and ethanol to a flask.
2. Dissolve sodium hydroxide in a little water and add it with stirring.
3. Add 1-bromobutane and fit a reflux condenser.
4. Heat at reflux for 2 hours.
5. Cool to room temperature.
6. Add water and transfer to a separatory funnel.

## Workup and Purification

Extract with ethyl acetate in portions, using 30 mL in total. Dry the combined organic layers over sodium sulfate, filter and evaporate the solvent to obtain the crude ether. Recrystallise from ethanol, filter and dry. Expected yield: 1.41 g (7.00 mmol, 70 %).

## Characterization

Colourless solid; expected ¹H NMR: δ 7.1–7.8 (m, 7H), 4.0 (t, 2H), 1.0–1.9 (m, 7H).

## Notes

1. The base converts 2-naphthol to its nucleophile; keep the mixture stirred during heating.
2. Check the identity and purity of the product before further use.

## Hazards and Waste Disposal

2-Naphthol: harmful if swallowed; irritant; 1-Bromobutane: flammable; harmful and irritating; suspected of causing genetic defects; Sodium hydroxide: causes severe burns; Ethanol: highly flammable; Ethyl acetate: highly flammable; eye irritant; Sodium sulfate: dust may irritate eyes; 2-Butoxynaphthalene: dust or vapour may irritate. Work in a fume hood with gloves and eye protection. Collect aqueous and organic waste separately according to local rules.
